title: Stop Prompting Claude. Use Karpathy's Method Instead.
registration: USER-RESERVED — derived during Phase 7 from Phase 3 transcript probe; no user pre-registration received

goldens.question: In Karpathy's car-wash example, how far is the car wash and what do state-of-the-art models incorrectly recommend?
goldens.expected_answer: 50 meters away; models recommend walking instead of driving.

goldens.question: What are the three layers of Karpathy's method described in this video?
goldens.expected_answer: The spec, the verifier, and the environment.

goldens.question: During the on-screen CLAUDE.md walkthrough (~9:31), what four section themes does the creator highlight?
goldens.expected_answer: How the repo works, custom skills and routing, knowledge/training-data architecture, and key working rules.

goldens.question: What does Karpathy say remains worth learning when intelligence gets cheap?
goldens.expected_answer: You can outsource thinking but not understanding; the layers center on your understanding of the bigger picture.

goldens.question: According to Boris Cherney (cited in the video), how much does a feedback loop improve Claude output quality?
goldens.expected_answer: Two to three times (2–3×) the quality of the final result.

goldens.question: What metaphor does the video use instead of Karpathy's 'ghosts' framing for why yelling at AI does not help?
goldens.expected_answer: A robot librarian — answers only from its library; confidently wrong when a book is missing.
